verdict: The Differential Engine is the MedKayfab series firing on all cylinders — 56 cards that teach probabilistic clinical reasoning through instantly performable wrestling personas. Named strength: the Bias Suite (cards 17-20, 37-40) is the most teachable run in any MedKayfab deck, with Anchor-the-Heavy and Silent-the-Stalker as standouts. Named weakness: Likeli-the-Ratio and Nomogram-the-Calculator (cards 21-22) are G3 deep-cuts that would benefit from a visual nomogram insert card. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 diagnostic reasoning wrestlers who teach you to think like a clinician — from Bayesian priors to cognitive bias traps. For med students, residents, and anyone who ever missed the zebra.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS – The Differential Engine (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master Bayesian priors, sensitivity versus specificity, and the cognitive biases that wreck a diagnosis long before the disease ever does.

Every other deck hands you a monster to beat. This one hands you a mirror. The disease is rarely what loses the match. What loses it is the prior you never checked, the first answer you fell in love with, the test you trusted without asking what it actually rules out. A clean exam and a confident read are exactly how the obvious case becomes the missed one, and no amount of extra facts saves you if the reasoning underneath is running the wrong move.

MedKayfab: The Differential Engine turns the invisible machinery of clinical reasoning into a narrative wrestling match, where every probability, every test characteristic, and every bias you carry steps into the ring as a fighter with a motive. Stop memorizing disease lists. Start running the engine that picks between them.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like RED-FLAG-REGGIE, Silent-the-Stalker, and The Dual-Diagnosis Duo
- A Final Quest meta-layer: Doc FrizzleBob plus three chained Quest scenarios that make you run the whole engine on one case
- Free lifetime updates as the evidence shifts
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the reasoning layer that sits under every specialty. You will meet RED-FLAG-REGGIE, the arena-stop who refuses to let the match continue until you prove the patient is not dying from something catastrophic. Silent-the-Stalker is the false negative made flesh, the test that reads clean while the disease quietly eats the health bar from the inside. The Dual-Diagnosis Duo is the case that breaks Occam's Razor, two problems wearing one set of symptoms. Behind them stand the villains you actually fight every shift: Anchor-the-Heavy, who locks the team onto the first impression and ignores every red flag after it, and Prematur-the-Closure, who rings the victory bell at the first explanation that happens to fit.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for high-stress retrieval. You have the Character (the reasoning move or the bias), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios), the Lore (why it wins or loses the match), and the Quest (the case it shows up in). The Mechanism Flash mode is unforgiving here: explain in one sentence why a negative test does or does not let you send the patient home, without looking, or the patient on the Stage pays for it. The Final Quest page is the synthesis bout, where System-1 the Flash, the biases, and the safety-nets all fight over the same case at once.

Honest cognitive load
This is a meta-engine, not a fact dump, so it rewards a little clinical exposure. It fits medical students moving into their clinical years, residents prepping for boards and OSCEs, and anyone who has both missed the zebra and chased one that was never there. It pairs naturally with Emergency Medicine for the same decisions under a running clock, with Internal Medicine for the multimorbid cases where two diagnoses hide behind one complaint, and with any organ-system deck whose look-alikes you keep confusing.
